text:
Alex Chen: Customer reported a spike of 502s and intermittent auth failures after they enabled the customer-managed gateway in their VPC. timeline: deploy at 10:05 UTC, errors at 10:07.
Jamie Patel: Which gateway stack are they running? envoy sidecar + nginx ingress, right?
Alex Chen: Yes — nginx ingress controller -> envoy sidecar -> customer proxy -> redwood private gateway. They say errors only when load hits ~400rps.
Maria Gomez: Any logs from envoy or the auth service? 502 usually from upstream error or HTTP/1.1 flapping.
Alex Chen: Pasted logs below from envoy at error time:
```
[2025-06-18T10:07:12.345Z] connection error: upstream reset before headers
upstream_host: 10.2.3.7:8080, code: 502
ratelimit: denied (global_quota_exceeded), token: abc.., route: /v1/generate
```
Kevin Liu: Interesting — envoy reports ratelimit denied and upstream reset. Could be their customer-managed rate-limiter returning 503 which envoy surfaces as 502 when upstream closed.
Jamie Patel: The customer mentioned auth tokens were failing too (401) in a follow-up. Could quota exhaustion of their auth service cause auth errors downstream?
Alex Chen: They also reported a billing spike from retries; their client retried on 502 which drove up usage and made the limiter hit the hard cap.
Maria Gomez: Can we get their envoy rate-limit config and their limiter's response codes? Also need their kube resource metrics at the time (cpu/memory of limiter pods)
Alex Chen: They attached the envoy filter snippet:
```
- name: envoy.filters.http.ratelimit
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ratelimit.v3.RateLimit
    domain: "redwood_ingress"
    timeout: 20s
```
and the rate-limit service is using token-bucket with "max_tokens": 200, "refill_rate": 100/s
```
rate_limit_service: {
  bucket: { capacity: 200, refill: 100 }
}
```
Kevin Liu: That capacity is small given they have many concurrent clients. If refill is per second and capacity 200, a short burst will drain it and return limit responses until refill.
Jamie Patel: What about their Kubernetes liveness readiness? If limiter pods restarted, there would be connection errors.
Alex Chen: Kube events show 3 restarts at 10:06:55 — OOMKilled on limiter-0. Memory was pinned at 95% before restart.
Maria Gomez: OOM explains sudden 503 from limiter. Envoy translates that to upstream reset/502 for the request. Auth failures could be from token cache flush during restart — auth service revalidated tokens against IdP and had rate limit too.
rate-limiter-bot: Detected repeated client retries pattern: exponential_backoff not enabled, retry_count=5, retry_interval=0.5s
Kevin Liu: That retry behavior would amplify load massively. Customer client should use 429/503 respect with jittered backoff.
Jamie Patel: Action plan:
1) Increase limiter pod memory + add HPA to scale on CPU/memory.
2) Increase token-bucket capacity temporarily to give headroom: capacity=2000, refill_rate=500/s.
3) Add a short 429->client guidance header and ensure clients honor Retry-After.
4) Add Envoy local rate-limit as soft guard before calling external limiter.
5) Recommend client retry policy: max_retries=2, backoff_base=200ms, jitter=50%
Alex Chen: I pushed a quick config to customer (suggested values above). Also asked them to enable envoy local_rate_limit with 1500rps per pod.
Maria Gomez: Also suggest improving auth token caching TTL and warming the cache during deploys to avoid thundering herd on IdP.
Kevin Liu: Follow-up for billing: we advised them to pause aggressive client retries and open a billing dispute ticket with our billing team; we can provide usage window and mitigation timeline.
Alex Chen: Customer applied memory bump and HPA. After that at 10:28 errors dropped to baseline. They still want guidance on long-term knob tuning for on-prem gateways.
Jamie Patel: Long-term recommendations (to paste to customer):
- Run limiter as statefulset with persistent cache or multi-replica in front of a shared Redis so restarts don't lose tokens.
- Add local ingress rate-limits in Envoy/nginx to shed traffic early.
- Use graceful shutdown hooks so limiter stops accepting new requests before pod termination.
- Implement token caching and backoff-aware clients.
Maria Gomez: I'll draft an ops playbook for them: healthchecks, alerts (OOM, restart_count > 1, 5xx spike), and a tuning checklist.
Alex Chen: Customer happy. They asked if we can provide a sample Envoy filter + token-bucket values for 1000rps sustained with 5k burst. I'll attach after this thread.
Jamie Patel: Nice. Can we add this thread as KB: support/rate-limiter-onprem-auth-spike-1758204321? If so, please redact customer identifiers.
Alex Chen: Will create KB and link it. Marking this thread resolved.
